newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends down on Hong Kong weakness.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends down on Hong Kong weakness.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares closed down nearly 4.6 percent on Tuesday, dragged lower by falls in Hong Kong-listed H shares, brokers said.
Sharp falls on Tuesday in H shares, or Chinese enterprises traded in Hong Kong, hurt sentiment for China plays, causing investors to sell B shares in Shanghai, brokers said.
The B index fell 4.057 points or 4.59 percent to 84.367 on turnover of $22.538 million compared with $30.000 million on Monday.
Both foreign and domestic investors sold B shares, which had registered sharp gains last week on a wave of foreign and Hong Kong liquidity, brokers said.
Falls in H shares as well as Hong Kong's broader market sparked fears foreign buying had played itself out for the time being, causing investors to flee B shares, they said.
Hong Kong stocks fell on jitters over a speculative attack on the local currency, as well as a sell-off in U.S. stocks on Friday. Wall Street recovered some of the losses on Monday.
"The (Friday) fall in the Dow Jones index brought down the Shanghai B share index," said one local broker.

Some market players also took profits after rumours that domestic investors soon would be allowed to buy B shares through the establishment of Sino-foreign joint venture funds failed to prove true, brokers said.
"The rumors weren't realised, which also hurt sentiment," said another local broker.

Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products Co was the biggest B share loser on Tuesday after last week announcing its first-half profits rose a lower-than-expected 5.8 percent. It slid $0.098 or 9.86 percent to $0.896 on volume of nearly 2.9 million shares, making it the second most active stock.
"If you look at the industry, there are indications that cashmere is hitting the top of its price cycle," said a broker at a foreign securities firm.
Of the 47 B share issues, 46 were traded on Tuesday with 43 of them losing ground. Two rose while one was unchanged.
Recently listed Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal Co was the most actively traded B share on profit-taking, brokers said. It fell $0.014 or 2.64 percent to $0.516.
Phoenix Bicycle was the second worst B share performer on the day, losing $0.014 or 9.72 percent to $0.130. Brokers said it has been weak of late on expectations of poor interim results.
Brokers said B shares could see further falls later this week, but they put firm support for the index around 80 and 81 points.
Shanghai's domestic currency A shares ended the day down slightly in dull trading with most investors clinging to the sidelines, they said.

The A index slipped 0.069 point or 0.01 percent to 1,179.373 on turnover of 2.157 billion yuan against 2.750 billion on Monday. The SSE30 blue chip index lost 2.471 points or 0.07 percent to 3,553.717 points.
Aluminium products maker Xinjiang Zhonghe was the biggest loser, tumbling 10.04 percent or 0.81 yuan to 7.25 yuan. It reported disappointing interim results.
